questions.q: Why is a parameterized query safe from SQL injection when an f-string building the same query is not?
options: Parameterized queries run faster, which prevents injection
The database driver sends the parameter as data, never interpreting it as SQL syntax, while an f-string splices the value directly into the SQL text
F-strings are deprecated in modern Python
Parameterized queries only work with SQLite
questions.explain: Injection happens when untrusted text is interpreted as SQL syntax. A parameterized query hands the value to the driver separately from the SQL text, so it can never be read as syntax no matter what characters it contains.

questions.q: If an AI data analyst's database role has only SELECT grants and no write or DDL grants, what's the worst a maliciously-crafted question could still do?
options: Drop every table in the database
Return wrong or unintended results, but not modify or destroy data
Change other users' passwords
Nothing -- a read-only role prevents all possible harm
questions.explain: A least-privilege, read-only role closes off destructive actions entirely, but a bad or unintended query can still return incorrect results -- that risk is addressed by validation in Lesson 10, not by the role itself.

questions.q: What problem does a statement timeout specifically guard against?
options: SQL injection through string concatenation
A generated query (e.g., an unintended cross join) scanning a huge table and hanging the connection
A user entering an invalid email address
The API call in Lesson 11 returning malformed JSON
questions.explain: A timeout turns a runaway query into a fast, visible failure instead of a stuck connection -- it doesn't prevent injection, which parameterization already handles.

questions.q: Why does this lesson build the safe database connection before Lesson 10 introduces any LLM-generated SQL?
options: Because LLMs cannot generate SQL at all
Because the connection itself must be unable to do damage regardless of what text ends up in a query, whether from a developer, a model, or an attacker
Because it's required by the SQL standard
Because read-only roles only work after a model is involved
questions.explain: Get the connection wrong and nothing built on top of it in later lessons is trustworthy -- the safety has to exist before the model is introduced, not after.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three defense-in-depth layers this lesson covers?
options: Parameterized queries
A least-privilege, read-only database role
A statement timeout and hard row limit
Encrypting the entire database at rest
questions.explain: This lesson's three layers are parameterized queries, a least-privilege role, and a statement timeout plus row limit. At-rest encryption is a real practice but isn't one covered in this lesson.
